subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The work of others and design strategies

questions.q: What is primary data in the context of designing?
options: Data collected first-hand by the designer, such as from a survey of users
Information taken from existing books and websites
Data that must always be presented as numbers
Historical sales figures found in a company's annual report
questions.explain: Primary data is original information gathered directly by the designer, for example through questionnaires, interviews or observation.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of secondary data?
options: Statistics found in a published market research report
Measuring the hand spans of ten users yourself
Interviewing potential customers face to face
Observing people using a product in a shop
questions.explain: Secondary data already exists and has been collected by someone else, such as published reports, books or websites.

questions.q: Why might a designer use both primary and secondary data during investigation?
options: Primary data gives specific, current user information while secondary data provides wider background context
Primary data is always wrong so secondary data corrects it
Secondary data is faster to collect but never reliable
Using both types is required by law before selling a product
questions.explain: Combining both gives a fuller, more balanced picture: targeted first-hand findings supported by existing wider research.

questions.q: Which statement about questionnaires is correct?
options: Closed questions produce data that is quicker and easier to analyse
Open questions always give data that is easier to turn into graphs
Questionnaires can only ever collect secondary data
A questionnaire cannot be used to gather user opinions
questions.explain: Closed questions limit responses to set options, making the results faster to count and compare than open-ended answers.

questions.q: A student designing a new school backpack wants first-hand information about what pupils dislike about their current bags. Which method provides primary data?
options: Handing out a questionnaire to pupils at the school
Reading online reviews of existing backpacks
Looking through a competitor's product catalogue
Studying a published market report on schoolbags
questions.explain: Asking pupils directly through a questionnaire gathers original, first-hand primary data about the actual users.

questions.q: Which set correctly lists the six Rs of sustainable design?
options: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink, Repair
Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Restore, Renew, Repair
Reduce, Remove, Recycle, Reject, Rethink, Reform
Reuse, Recycle, Reduce, Reboot, Repair, Return
questions.explain: The six Rs used to reduce environmental impact are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, Refuse, Rethink and Repair.

questions.q: What does the abbreviation LCA stand for when assessing a product's environmental impact?
options: Life Cycle Assessment
Long-term Cost Analysis
Low Carbon Approach
Lifetime Consumer Audit
questions.explain: A Life Cycle Assessment examines a product's environmental impact across its whole life, from raw materials to disposal.

questions.q: In the six Rs, what does 'Reduce' mean?
options: Using fewer materials or less energy to make and run a product
Repairing a broken product so it can keep being used
Turning old products into new raw materials
Refusing to buy products that are not needed
questions.explain: 'Reduce' means cutting down on the materials, energy or resources a product uses, lowering its environmental impact.

questions.q: What is meant by 'planned obsolescence'?
options: Designing a product with a deliberately limited lifespan so it needs replacing
Designing a product that can be endlessly repaired and upgraded
Planning production carefully to avoid wasting materials
Making a product from fully recyclable materials
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence deliberately shortens a product's useful life, encouraging repeat purchases but increasing waste.

questions.q: A designer redesigns a drinks bottle so it uses 30 per cent less plastic while working just as well. Which of the six Rs does this best demonstrate?
options: Reduce
Refuse
Reuse
Repair
questions.explain: Using less material to achieve the same function is a clear example of 'Reduce'.

questions.q: Harry Beck is best known for designing which of the following?
options: The London Underground map
The Mini car
The Juicy Salif lemon squeezer
The Red and Blue Chair
questions.explain: Harry Beck designed the iconic diagrammatic London Underground map, first published in 1933.

questions.q: The bagless vacuum cleaner using cyclone technology is most associated with which designer or company?
options: Dyson
Braun
Alessi
Zara
questions.explain: James Dyson developed the bagless vacuum cleaner that uses cyclone technology to separate dust from the air.

questions.q: What is 'design fixation'?
options: Becoming stuck on existing ideas or solutions, which limits creativity
Fixing all the dimensions of a design before making it
A method of firmly attaching components together
Copying a design exactly to save development time
questions.explain: Design fixation is when a designer becomes locked into familiar solutions, preventing more original ideas from emerging.

questions.q: What best describes 'user-centred design'?
options: A design approach that focuses on the needs and wants of the end user throughout the process
A strategy of designing whatever is cheapest to manufacture
Designing only from the designer's own personal preferences
Basing all decisions on secondary data alone
questions.explain: User-centred design keeps the end user's needs central at every stage, often involving them in testing and feedback.

questions.q: A design team hold regular meetings with a materials engineer and a marketing specialist while developing a product. Which design strategy does this show?
options: Collaboration
Design fixation
Planned obsolescence
Secondary research
questions.explain: Working with specialists from different fields to share expertise is an example of collaboration.

questions.q: How does an isometric drawing represent a product?
options: In 3D, with vertical lines kept vertical and other lines drawn at 30 degrees to the horizontal
Flat, in two dimensions only
In 3D, with all lines meeting at a single vanishing point
Split apart to show every internal component separately
questions.explain: Isometric drawings show objects in 3D using 30-degree angles, keeping vertical edges vertical and lines to scale.

questions.q: What is an exploded drawing mainly used to show?
options: How the separate parts of a product fit together
The exact colour and surface finish of a product
The market price of a finished product
A product's environmental impact over its life
questions.explain: An exploded view separates the components along their assembly lines to show how they connect together.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of making a prototype during development?
options: To test and evaluate a design so it can be improved before final production
To provide the finished product for immediate sale
To replace the need for any user feedback
To lower the cost of raw materials
questions.explain: Prototypes let designers test, evaluate and refine ideas, supporting an iterative approach before committing to production.

questions.q: What does an orthographic (working) drawing typically show?
options: Front, side and plan views drawn to scale with dimensions
A single 3D pictorial view with a vanishing point
A rough freehand impression of a concept
A mood board of colours and textures
questions.explain: Orthographic working drawings present accurate, scaled 2D views (front, side and plan) with dimensions for manufacture.

questions.q: A designer needs to communicate the exact dimensions of a component to a manufacturer. Which is the most appropriate drawing type?
options: A dimensioned orthographic working drawing
A quick freehand perspective sketch
A mood board of design influences
An isometric concept sketch without measurements
questions.explain: A dimensioned orthographic working drawing gives precise, scaled measurements needed to manufacture a component accurately.
